text:
# Cooperative Scheduling and Synchronization

Also called: Cooperative Scheduling, Synchronization for Backward Pass

## Overview
Cooperative Scheduling and Synchronization addresses idle resources and gradient contention caused by uneven tile lists, variable pixel traversal, and backward propagation accumulation [S1, unofficial]. It sets itself apart from static [mapping strategies](#9321-mapping-strategies.md) by dynamically redistributing work and organizing computation to minimize global atomic updates, replacing them with local reductions or cache-cooperative operations [S1, unofficial], contrasting with [Adaptive View and Pixel Sampling Scheduling](15689-adaptive-view-and-pixel-sampling-scheduling.md) which optimizes sampling patterns rather than compute scheduling.

## Shared principles
The core mechanism relies on two primary optimizations to handle the irregularity of 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) [rasterization](#15310-rasterization.md):

1. **Dynamic Work Redistribution:** Static mappings of Gaussians to tiles or pixels are prone to warp divergence due to footprint coverage and [early termination](#4675-early-termination.md) [S1, unofficial]. Cooperative scheduling dynamically assigns tiles or Gaussians to threads/warps to balance the load, ensuring that resources remain active even when the number of pairs ($N_{pair}$) and evaluations ($N_{eval}$) is unchanged [S1, unofficial].
2. **Local Gradient Reduction:** Backward propagation requires accumulating gradients from many pixels into each Gaussian [S1, unofficial]. Instead of performing frequent global atomic updates, these methods organize computation to combine gradients locally (within a warp, tile, or Gaussian-centric block) before writing the final result back to global memory [S1, unofficial]. This reduces global atomic contention [S1, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### Balanced 3DGS
Redistributes work through [dynamic tile assignment](#13381-load-balancing-strategy-for-multicomputer-volume-rendering.md) and enables Gaussian [parallel rendering](#9364-parallel-rendering-hybrid-systems.md) inside a warp. Not given in the sources. See [Balanced 3DGS](10236-balanced-3dgs.md).

### Local-GS
Uses parameter hoisting, warp culling, and coherent blending to reuse data and coordinate pixel processing within tiles. Not given in the sources. See [Local-GS](10237-local-gs.md).

### DISTWAR
Combines warp reduction with cache cooperation to reduce global atomic updates and contention during backward propagation. Not given in the sources. See [DISTWAR](10238-distwar.md).

### Taming 3DGS
Organizes backward computation around Gaussians, combining gradients before writing them back, replacing some global updates with local reduction. Not given in the sources. See [Taming 3DGS](10239-taming-3dgs.md).

### Faster-GS
Combines a refined Gaussian-centric backward pass with a parameter layout that keeps spatially nearby Gaussians close in memory, reducing global updates and enabling more regular reads. Not given in the sources. See [Faster-GS](10240-faster-gs.md).

## Background
The concept emerged as a response to the inefficiencies of static rasterization schedules in 3D Gaussian Splatting [S1, unofficial]. Uneven tile lists and variable pixel traversal leave GPU resources idle [S1, unofficial]. The approach was developed by multiple independent research groups to optimize both forward and backward passes:
* **Balanced 3DGS** [15] introduced dynamic tile assignment [S1, unofficial].
* **[Local-GS](#23282-local-gs.md)** [62] focused on warp-level coordination [S1, unofficial].
* **DISTWAR** [17] targeted backward propagation contention [S1, unofficial].
* **[Taming 3DGS](#8058-taming-3dgs.md)** [63] reorganized backward computation around Gaussians [S1, unofficial].
* **Faster-GS** [64] optimized parameter layout for spatial locality [S1, unofficial].

These methods are cited in the broader survey "From Splats to Silicon: Rethinking Computational Efficiency of 3DGS" [S1, unofficial].

## Sources
